before: A rich paste named a place only at a slot and only for a one-paragraph fragment, so a fragment with paragraphs, or any fragment at a caret mid-way through an inline control, was refused as indivisible content; a copy ending at a paragraph's end always carried its mark.
after: A rich paste names the caret's place as typing does and lands inside an inline control as one sentence, a host paste policy may rewrite the blocks and refuse the result, a copy carries the last mark only with the whole paragraph, and a host may meet prompts with a caret.
reason: The landing is resolved locally into the same transaction and published as its ordinary primitives; no operation, field or shared update format changes, and a peer replays the result unchanged.
